1.

The petitioner is seeking compensation in the wake of Detailed Accident Report (DAR) filed by police corresponding to the investigation carried out in case FIR No.
971/18 U/s 279/338 IPC registered at PS. S.P. Badli, with regard to Motor Vehicular Accident which occurred on 22.12.2018 at about 9:40 PM in front of BG Block, SGT Nagar, Delhi, involving Truck bearing registration no. DL1GC-6171(offending vehicle)
being driven by respondent no. 1 in a rash and negligent manner.

DAR filed by police,
was treated as claim petition under Section 166(4) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'MV Act').
2.
According to DAR, on 22.12.2018, the petitioner was going to his duty on motorcycle bearing registration no. DL11-SX-7238.

At about 9:30 PM, when he was crossing BG Block from the side of AG Block SGT Nagar, one truck bearing registration no. DL1GC-6171 which was being driven by MACP No. 331/21; FIR No. 971/18.; PS. S.P. Badli DOD: 06.06.2023 its driver at a very high speed,
in a rash and negligent manner, came and hit against the motorcycle of petitioner with a great force,
as a result of which he fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries.
Thereafter, petitioner was taken to Parnami Orthopedic Hospital, where he was medically examined vide MLC No. 115/18.
The offending vehicle was found to be owned by respondent no. 2 and insured with Oriental Insurance Company Ltd /respondent no. 3 during the period in question.
3. The respondents no. 1 & 2 i.e., driver and owner have failed to file their WS despite grant of sufficient time and opportunity.
4. The respondent no. 3 i.e., insurance company filed its legal offer of Rs.85,000/- which was not acceptable to the petitioner and the matter was proceeded on merits.

5. From the pleadings of the parties, the following issues were framed vide order dated 13.05.2022 passed by my Ld. Predecessor:-
1.

Whether the injured Kuldeep Singh suffered injuries in road traffic accident on 22.12.2018 at 21:40 hrs in front of BG Block, SGT Nagar, Delhi, within the jurisdiction of PS. S.P. Badli, due to rashness and negligence on the part of Sh.
Davinder Kumar who was driving truck bearing registration no. DL1GC-6171, owned by Sh. Gurcharan Singh and insured with The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd?
OPP MACP No. 331/21; FIR No. 971/18.; PS. S.P. Badli DOD: 06.06.2023 2.
Whether the injured is entitled to any compensation if so to what amount and from whom?

OPP.
3. Relief.

sentences.text: During his cross-examination on behalf of insurance company
, he deposed that at the relevant time, he was going from Sameypur Badli to Sanjay Gandhi Transport Nagar.
He further deposed that the offending truck, the number of which he did not remember was coming from the opposite direction.
He further deposed that he had seen the truck coming from opposite direction at about a distance of 45m being driven in a zigzag manner.
He deposed that he had stopped his motorcycle on his side of the road, yet the truck had hit him.
He admitted that there was no traffic signal at that spot indicating to stop the vehicle.
He denied the suggestion that the accident was caused due to his own rash and negligent driving as he stopped his vehicle in the middle of the road and accident was a head on collision.

11. It is evident from the testimony of PW1 that the respondent insurance company could not impeach his testimony through litmus test of cross-examination and said witness is found to have successfully withstood the test of cross-examination.
Even otherwise, PW1 himself is the injured having sustained injuries due to the accident in question.

Moreover, FIR No. 971/2018(Ex. PW1/6)
is shown to have been registered on the statement of petitioner himself.
The contents of said FIR would show that the complainant/petitioner has disclosed therein the same sequence of facts leading to the accident as deposed by him as PW1 in his evidence.
Hence, there is no possibility of any false implication of driver of offending vehicle or false involvement of the said vehicle in this case.
On the other hand, none of the respondents examined any witness in order to rebut the testimony of MACP No. 331/21; FIR No. 971/18.; PS. S.P. Badli DOD: 06.06.2023 PW1 during the course of inquiry.

Hence, there is no reason to disbelieve his uncontroverted testimony on the point of accident in question being caused by respondent no. 1 while driving the offending vehicle in a rash and negligent manner.

12. No doubt, the accident in question had occurred on 22.12.2018 and FIR in the matter was registered on 26.12.2018, however, in my opinion the said delay has been sufficiently explained by PW-1/petitioner/injured.
It is a matter of record that PW-1 remained under treatment from the date of accident till lodging of FIR.

The first priority for the petitioner/injured was to get himself medically treated, which he did and as soon as he got recovered to some extent from the injuries suffered by him, he got the FIR registered in the matter.

13. Be that as it may, GD No. 006A regarding accident victim being admitted to hospital was recorded in PS. S.P. Badli, on the basis of a call received from caller on 23.12.2018 at 8:38 AM(accident being caused on 22.12.2018 at about 9:30 PM).

Thus, it follows from the aforesaid discussion that the accident in question had taken place while respondent no. 1 was driving the offending vehicle at a very high speed and he could not keep control over the offending vehicle and ultimately, hit against the motorcycle of petitioner.
The facts and circumstances as brought on record, would show that said vehicle was being driven at very high speed due to which respondent MACP No. 331/21; FIR No. 971/18.;
PS . S.P. Badli DOD: 06.06.2023 no. 1 could not manage to stop the vehicle, which resulted into the accident in question.

14. In the aforesaid facts and circumstances where the cogent explanation has been furnished about the delay in the registration of FIR in criminal case, same cannot be considered to be fatal for the case of claimant in present proceedings.

Even otherwise, it is well settled law that delay in lodging Kuldeep Singh vs Davinder Kumar on 6 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142901653/
4 FIR cannot be a ground to throw away the case of claimant in such like proceedings in the backdrop of the conditions prevailing in our society where one cannot expect common man to rush to police station for registration of FIR immediately after the accident.

While saying so, I am fortified by the observations made by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in case titled as "Ravi V/s Badri Narayan &
Ors.", Civil Appeal No. 1926/2011, decided on 18.02.2011.

The intent and objective of the Beneficial Legislation is to grant equitable compensation to the vulnerable victims of road accidents and dynamic law has evolved towards grant of just and fair quantum of awards and has brought consistency and uniformity towards the desired goal.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in "Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation" (2009) 6 SCC 121, which was affirmed by a bench of three Hon'ble Judges in Reshma Kumari & Ors. Vs. Madan Mohan & Anr.,
(2013) 9 SCC 65, held as under:

sentences.text: "Just compensation" is adequate compensation which is fair and equitable, on the facts and circumstances of the case, to make good the loss suffered as a result of the wrong, as far as money can do so, by applying the well settled principles relating to award of compensation.
It is not intended to be a bonanza, largesse or source of profit.
17. Assessment of compensation though involving certain hypothetical considerations, should nevertheless be objective.
Justice and justness emanate from equality in treatment, consistency and thoroughness in adjudication, and fairness and uniformity in the decision making process and the decisions.
While it may not be possible to have mathematical precision or identical awards, in assessing compensation, same or similar facts should lead to awards in the same range.

When the factors/inputs are the same, and the formula/legal principles are the same,
consistency and uniformity, and not divergence and freakiness, should be the result of adjudication to arrive at just compensation..."
22.

These guiding principles for assessment of "just and reasonable compensation"
have been torch bearer in injury cases also as laid down by Hon'ble Delhi High Court,
in III (2007), ACC 676 titled as Oriental Insurance Co,. Ltd., Vs. Vijay Kumar Mittal & Ors, wherein it has been held:-
"10.

The possession of one's own body is the first and most valuable all human rights and while awarding compensation for bodily injuries this MACP No. 331/21; FIR No.
971/18.; PS. S.P. Badli DOD: 06.06.2023 primary element is to be kept in mind.
Bodily injury is to be treated and varies on account of gravity of bodily injury.

Though it is impossible to equate money with human suffering, agony and personal deprivation, the Court and Tribunal should make an honest and serious attempt to award damages so far as money can compensate the loss.
Regard must be given to the gravity and degree of deprivation as well as the degree of awareness of the deprivation.
Damages awarded in personal injury cases must be substantial and not token damages....."

24. Accordingly, the entitlement of petitioner to just compensation is being assessed in the background of well settled parameters and guidelines as discussed herein-above.
MEDICAL EXPENSES 25.

The petitioner has deposed in his evidence by way of affidavit(Ex. PW1/A) that after the accident, he was taken to Parnami Hospital, Delhi, where he was medically examined vide MLC No.
115/18.
He further deposed that he was admitted in the aforesaid hospital on 22.12.2018 and was discharged on 27.12.2018.
He has relied upon medical bills Ex. PW1/5(colly).
During his cross-examination on behalf of insurance company, he admitted that the medical bills and the bills for purchase of medicines were not supported by the prescription of the doctor.
He volunteered that whatever medical record he possessed, had been filed on record.
MACP No. 331/21; FIR No. 971/18.; PS. S.P. Badli DOD: 06.06.2023 26.

It is relevant to note that the injured has relied upon medical bills amounting to Rs. 1,46,570/-
(which are Ex. PW1/5 colly).

It is not out of place to mention that the respondent insurance company has not been able to dispute the authenticity and genuineness of the medical bills filed on record during the course of inquiry.
They have also not led any evidence in rebuttal so as to create any doubt on the genuineness of said bills.
Accordingly, a sum of Rs. 1,46,570/- is awarded to the petitioner under this head.

per month.

28. During the course of arguments, Ld. Counsel for injured argued that due to the injuries suffered by him, he could not work for considerable period and thus, he has suffered loss of income and as such, appropriate compensation shall be awarded to the petitioner under this head.
MACP No. 331/21; FIR No. 971/18.; PS. S.P. Badli DOD: 06.06.2023 29.
The treatment record i.e., Discharge Summary (Ex. PW1/3) of Parnami Hospital of petitioner shows that he was admitted in said hospital on 22.12.2018 and was discharged on 27.12.2018.
As per the aforesaid treatment record, the case of petitioner was of comminuted fracture shaft tibia left.
It is also apparent from the treatment record that closed reduction and internal fixation with interlocking nailing left tibia was done on 23.12.2018.
Apart from the aforesaid document, the petitioner has failed to file any other treatment record.

In the absence of any definite evidence being brought on record showing the actual period till which the petitioner had received medical treatment for the injuries sustained by him due to accident in question, it would necessarily involve some guess work in assessing the loss of income.
It can not be overlooked that the petitioner had sustained grievous injuries in the accident in question.
Apart from this petitioner has also suffered permanent disability to the extent of 12% in relation to left lower limb.

Considering the nature of injuries and permanent disability suffered by the petitioner, it is presumed that he would not have been able to work at least for a period of 5 months or so including his recovery period.
30. It may be noted here that petitioner has relied upon one document Mark B in order to substantiate his plea that he was earning Rs. 15,000/- per month at the time of accident.

However,
no definite evidence whatsoever has been brought on record to prove the said document in respect of monthly income of injured/petitioner at the time of accident in question.
Petitioner has also failed to file his educational qualification documents.
MACP No. 331/21; FIR No. 971/18.; PS. S.P. Badli DOD: 06.06.2023
Thus, his loss of income has to be assessed while taking the income of an unskilled person under Minimum Wages Act applicable during the period in question.
The minimum wages of an unskilled person were Rs. 14,000/- per month as on the date of accident which is 22.12.2018.
Thus, a sum of Rs. 70,000/- (Rs. 14,000/- x 5) is awarded in favour of petitioner under this head.

32. As already considered, the petitioner suffered comminuted fracture shaft tibia left and remained incapacitated to resume his work of earnings for a period of about 5 months owing to grievous injuries suffered in the road traffic accident.
Apart from this, the petitioner is also shown to have sustained permanent disability to the extent of 12% in relation to his left lower limb.
Thus, he would have undergone great physical sufferings, inconvenience and mental trauma on account of the accident in question.

Keeping in view the nature of injuries suffered by the petitioner, duration of treatment and permanent disability suffered by him, a sum of Rs. 70,000/- is considered reasonable towards pain & sufferings.
LOSS OF GENERAL AMENITIES & ENJOYMENT OF LIFE 33.
As already mentioned above, there is sufficient evidence on record to establish that the petitioner had sustained grievous injuries in the accident.
Apart from this, the petitioner is also shown to have sustained permanent disability to the extent of 12% in relation to his left lower limb.
Thus, he would not be able to enjoy general amenities of life after the accident in question and his quality of life has been definitely affected.

In view of the nature of injuries suffered by him and permanent disability MACP No. 331/21; FIR No. 971/18.; PS. S.P. Badli DOD: 06.06.2023 suffered by him, I award a notional sum of Rs. 50,000/- towards loss of general amenities and enjoyment of life to the petitioner.
